feasibility_limit: Target-native execution was unavailable in the scout environment. These cases define required traces and distinguishing outcomes for owned-fork adapters.

stimulus: one or more assistant/tool events occur
OpenCode reports turn completion or session idle
invariants: final T3 status is not running or starting
final activeTurnId is null
the browser accepts a subsequent user turn
restart does not restore the completed turn to running

distinguishing_outcomes.adapter_loss: Provider completion exists but no canonical T3 event is emitted.
distinguishing_outcomes.guard_rejection: Canonical completion exists but lifecycle correlation rejects it.
distinguishing_outcomes.projection_regression: Completion is applied and a later update restores stale running state.
distinguishing_outcomes.pass: Provider, canonical, persisted, and client states converge on ready/idle.

invariants: provider truth is consulted before indefinitely disabling input
stale activeTurnId is cleared or the thread is marked explicitly degraded
the user receives a recoverable state rather than permanent working

stimulus: call ProviderService.interruptTurn for the old turn
observations: whether new provider events or side effects occur
how the controller reports the result
invariants: interruption does not resume work unless the provider contract explicitly requires it
any required recovery is visible and bound to the exact old turn
no new active turn is created

stimulus: registry closes the old child scope
invariants: the old terminal event is retained or an explicit interrupted/degraded event is persisted
the thread does not remain falsely running
events from old and new instance identities cannot be conflated

stimulus: attach after the oldest output has been trimmed
invariants: attachment reports the earliest retained absolute cursor or an explicit gap flag
client can distinguish complete replay from a surviving suffix
replay begins on a valid Unicode boundary

stimulus: continue PTY output without activating or detaching subscriber
invariants: pending subscriber state has a documented bound, timeout, or forced detachment
one inactive client cannot grow memory without limit
active clients continue receiving output

stimulus: submit an approval or user-input response using the old request id
invariants: the request is still pending
request, provider instance, session, and turn identities all match
expired or completed requests are rejected
a response cannot create a new unrelated turn

stimulus: ingest both events in the stated order
invariants: a delayed event cannot restore the completed turn to running
turn identity and sequence are used when available
ambiguous stale events are logged or quarantined
